svg.title: The Thirteen Colonies, 1763 Proclamation Line & American Crisis (1763–1783)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of Eastern North America (1763–1783) showing the Thirteen British Atlantic Colonies, British Canada and Nova Scotia, the Indigenous Reserve west of King George III’s 1763 Royal Proclamation Line along the Appalachian Mountains, Boston Harbour and Lexington, Philadelphia (1776), Virginia and the Siege of Yorktown (1781), and the 1783 Book of Negroes Black Loyalist evacuation from New York to Birchtown, Nova Scotia.

text.tspan: Appalachians block settler westward land grab
1783 Book of Negroes evacuates 3,000 Black Loyalists
Paine’s Common Sense & Declaration of Independence

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: THE FIRST BRITISH EMPIRE (1600–1783)
The Thirteen Colonies, 1763 Proclamation Line & American Crisis (1763–83)
Britain’s 1763 Appalachian land ban and taxes without representation ignited protest in Boston and independence in 1776.
Cornwallis’s 1781 surrender at Yorktown ended Britain’s First Empire in America while 3,000 Black Loyalists sailed to Nova Scotia.
